chunks: From him, from Faḍālah, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Muḥammad ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Abī al-Ward, who said:

I said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Abū Ẓabyān narrated to me that he saw ʿAlī عليه السلام pour water and then wipe over the khuffs. So he said: “Abū Ẓabyān lied. Has the statement of ʿAlī عليه السلام not reached you among yourselves: ‘The Book has preceded the khuffs’?”
Then I said: Is there any concession in it? He said: “No, except against an enemy from whom you are protecting yourself, or snow such that you fear for your feet.”

key_terms.الْخُفَّيْنِ: the two khuffs; leather footwear worn over the feet
key_terms.ثَلْجٍ: snow; severe cold cited as an exceptional circumstance
key_terms.رُخْصَةٌ: a concession or legal dispensation in a case of hardship
key_terms.رِجْلَيْكَ: your two feet; the body part directly affected by the ruling
key_terms.سَبَقَ الْكِتَابُ الْخُفَّيْنِ: the Book has precedence over the khuffs; meaning the Qur'anic ruling takes priority regarding wudu (ablution)
key_terms.عَدُوٍّ: an enemy; a situation of danger or threat
key_terms.مَسَحَ: wiped; here, wiping in the context of wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: Is wiping over khuffs permitted in wudu (ablution) according to this hadith from Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that wiping over the khuffs in wudu (ablution) is not accepted as a normal ruling, and it attributes this position to ʿAlī عليه السلام. It allows only a limited concession in cases of fear from an enemy or severe cold that may harm the feet.
